entities.summary: Juan Carlos Blanco Fernández was a Uruguayan political figure and education advocate who played a pivotal role in shaping Uruguay's educational system during the late 19th century. As the president of the National Assembly, he spearheaded the creation of the first national education law, which aimed to increase access to education for all Uruguayans. This legislation, enacted in 1889, had a lasting impact on the country's education system, leading to the expansion of primary education and the establishment of a national network of schools. Blanco Fernández's efforts also contributed to the development of Uruguay's national identity and its position as a leader in education reform in Latin America. The Uruguay round of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), held in 1994, marked a significant turning point in the country's economic history, as it led to the country's entry into the international trade arena and the adoption of a more liberal trade policy. Blanco Fernández's legacy can be seen in the continued emphasis on education as a key driver of national development and the ongoing efforts to promote social justice and equality through education. The country's commitment to social welfare and public education remains a cornerstone of its social policy, reflecting Blanco Fernández's commitment to the principles of democracy and social justice.
